pcs.pc_description: Comprehend the company priorities to have a clear idea of the objectives of the business.

pcs.pc_description: Research and understand current and projected clean electricity market prices.
Formulate a clear negotiation strategy outlining desired outcomes regarding pricing, contract terms, and sustainability commitments.
Communicate the anticipated volume and profile of clean electricity required for green hydrogen production throughout the contract term.
Negotiate a contract term that aligns with the green hydrogen production project timeline and provides enough stability for a clean electricity supply.
Devise concise Service Level Agreements (SLAs) outlining guaranteed uptime, power quality standards, and response times for potential disruptions.
Discuss the possibility of including clauses encouraging the supplier to invest in further renewable energy development or sustainable practices in their electricity generation processes.
Carefully review the finalised contract to ensure all agreed-upon terms are accurately reflected.
Analyse the clean electricity demand for green hydrogen production and assess the existing grid infrastructure's capacity to handle the additional load.
Identify the closest grid interconnection point and evaluate the feasibility of connecting the green hydrogen production facility.
Work with the grid operator to finalise a formal grid interconnection agreement.
Negotiate fair and transparent fees for grid interconnection, considering factors like distance to the grid point, required infrastructure upgrades, and long-term benefits for the grid.
Collect and analyse procurement data using software like SAP Ariba, Coupa, Jaggaer, Oracle Procurement Cloud, etc., to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.
Develop criteria for supplier selection, including sustainability and ethical considerations with a focus on Renewable Energy Source (RES) integration and Green Hydrogen Guarantees of Origin (GoO).
Conduct thorough evaluations of potential suppliers, including site visits and audits, ensuring compliance with ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 standards.
Assess the financial stability and reputation of potential suppliers.
Verify supplier credentials, certifications, and compliance with regulatory standards.
Confirm that the suppliers meet environmental and social responsibility criteria.
Ensure suppliers adhere to fair labour practices and human rights standards.
Prepare negotiation strategies to achieve the best terms and conditions, considering contract clauses for Renewable Power Purchase Agreements (PPA) and Green Hydrogen Offtake Agreements.
Ensure contracts include clear terms on quality, delivery schedules, and penalties for non- compliance.
Determine critical performance metrics such as responsiveness, delivery, quality, cost reduction, etc. and clearly outline processes to track performance.
Ensure that supplier performance metrics are SMART (specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-based) and based on business needs.
Implement performance monitoring systems to track supplier performance against agreed metrics.

modules.module_title: Finalise negotiation and proceed with the order

pcs.pc_description: Collaborate with internal sales and customer service teams to gather detailed green hydrogen order requirements, including desired volume, delivery schedule, and any specific quality certifications needed.
Analyse demand forecasts and green hydrogen production capacity to assess the feasibility of fulfilling the requested order quantities within the desired timeframe.
Negotiate realistic delivery schedules with the customer, considering feasibility assessments, potential lead times, and any identified risks.
Collaborate with logistics teams to understand available transportation options and associated costs based on the negotiated delivery schedule (e.g., expedited vs. standard shipping).

Negotiate contract terms with suppliers that ensure flexibility in order fulfilment, including options for adjusting order quantities within a pre- defined window or utilising alternative transportation routes if necessary.

Document all agreed-upon terms for order fulfilment, including quantities, delivery schedule, pricing, and any specific quality requirements in a formal contract with the chosen supplier and customer.

modules.module_title: Conduct a risk assessment of suppliers

pcs.pc_description: Conduct risk assessments to identify potential risks in procurement activities.
Analyse the risk factors most relevant to the business/company .
Assess potential risks such as supply shortages, price volatility, and regulatory changes.
Classify the various risks associated with suppliers, such as financial risks, legal risks, risks in terms of image, etc.
Identify the suppliers who pose the most significant risk to the organisation.
Correlate the different data types to be collected for supplier risk assessment, such as supplier financial score, business continuity plans, Q S audits, lead time analysis, etc.

Develop suitable financial and non-financial risk assessment metrics such as order lead time, variance against budget, customer query time, delivery performance, pricing against market, etc., based on company objectives, culture, technology, and critical parameters.
Conduct a focused review of suppliers against the pre-determined risk assessment metrics.
Analyse the result of risk assessment and segment each supplier into risk categories such as high risk, medium risk and low risk.
Identify the attributes that are driving the risk rating and deploy strategies to mitigate risk in each category.
Deploy contingency plans and increase focus on high-risk suppliers.

Apply increased frequency and scrutiny of monitoring risk indicator trends such as frequent price hikes, lending institutions have significantly reduced supplier's line of credit, etc., for medium- risk suppliers.
Implement increased dialogue with supplier management for medium-risk suppliers.
Execute firm enforcement of terms and document variances at each level of suppliers.
Evaluate the impact and likelihood of identified risks.
Create risk mitigation plans to address identified risks.
Implement measures to minimise the effects of risks on procurement activities.
Regularly update risk management plans to match ISO 31000 guidelines as conditions change.
Ensure all GH2 procurement follows risk management guidelines to promote a culture that is aware of risks within the organisation.

modules.module_title: Compliance with GH2 Regulations and Standards

pcs.pc_description: Stay informed about the latest hydrogen production, storage, and distribution regulations.
Keep away any ignition sources from hydrogen storage areas and maintain a strict no- smoking policy within this zone.
Follow signage and warnings for usage of hazardous areas and equipment.
Always wear appropriate cryogenic protective clothing, gloves and equipment when handling liquid hydrogen.
Report any non-compliance issues promptly to relevant personnel.
Adhere to safety protocols when using materials, tools, and equipment for handling GH2.
Follow established safety procedures for working with hydrogen, including permit systems,lockout/tagout procedures, and access controls.
Activate alarms and evacuate personnel according to emergency plans, ensuring everyone's safety.
Provide clear and concise information about the incident to the emergency responders and rescue personnel.
Participate in regular emergency response drills and training, demonstrating competence and composure in simulated scenarios.
Use appropriate fire extinguishers compatible with hydrogen and fire hoses to isolate the fire at the source.
Respond promptly and effectively to emergencies and potential hydrogen leaks, including evacuation procedures, communication with emergency services, and implementation of emergency response plans.
Follow first aid instructions according to the type of injury/ incident.
Move yourself or the injured person away from the source of the cryogenic liquid or gas to stop further exposure.
